url-parser.name: URL Parser
url-parser.tagline: Parse, inspect, and edit URLs and query parameters.
url-parser.metaTitle: URL Parser - Parse & Edit Query Parameters Free Online
url-parser.metaDescription: Parse any URL into protocol, host, path, and query params. Edit parameters visually and rebuild the URL. Free, no signup, runs in your browser.
url-parser.keywords: url parser, parse url online, query parameter editor, url decoder, inspect url parts
url-parser.quickAnswer: Paste any URL and this tool breaks it into its parts: protocol, host, port, path, hash, and every query parameter. You can edit parameter names and values directly, add or remove parameters, then rebuild a clean, properly encoded URL with one click.
keyFacts: A URL has the structure scheme://host:port/path?query#fragment, defined by RFC 3986.
Query parameters are key=value pairs separated by & after the ? character.
Special characters in parameters are percent-encoded, for example a space becomes %20.
The fragment (after #) is never sent to the server; it is handled by the browser.
Editing parameters here re-encodes them automatically, so the rebuilt URL is always valid.
howTo: Paste a URL into the input field.
Click Parse to split it into parts and parameters.
Edit any parameter name or value inline.
Add new parameters or remove ones you do not need.
Click Rebuild URL to get the updated, encoded URL, then copy it.
url-parser.formula:
URL = scheme "://" host [":" port] path ["?" query] ["#" fragment]
Example: https://shop.example.com:443/search?q=shoes&color=red#top
protocol=https host=shop.example.com port=443 path=/search params={q: shoes, color: red} hash=top
url-parser.workedExample:
Parsing https://jaurtools.com/en/url-parser?tool=url&utm_source=google#features gives:
protocol: https, host: jaurtools.com, port: (none), path: /en/url-parser, hash: features
parameters: tool=url, utm_source=google
Changing utm_source to newsletter and clicking Rebuild produces:
https://jaurtools.com/en/url-parser?tool=url&utm_source=newsletter#features
benefits: See every part of a URL at a glance, no manual splitting.
Edit query strings visually without encoding mistakes.
Useful for debugging tracking parameters and API calls.
limitations: Only absolute URLs with a scheme (http/https) can be parsed.
Very long URLs over 2000 characters are truncated.
The tool validates structure, not whether the URL actually exists.
Internationalized domain names are shown in punycode form.

faqs.a: A key=value pair in the part of the URL after the ? mark. Servers and apps read these to customize the response, like ?page=2 or ?lang=ar.

faqs.q: Why do I see %20 in URLs?
faqs.a: That is percent-encoding: characters unsafe in URLs are replaced with % plus their hex code. A space becomes %20. The rebuild step applies this automatically.

faqs.q: Can I parse a URL without https://?
faqs.a: No. The parser needs an absolute URL with a scheme. Add https:// in front of domain-only input before parsing.

faqs.q: Is the fragment sent to the server?
faqs.a: No. Everything after # stays in the browser and is never included in the HTTP request.

faqs.q: Does editing parameters encode special characters?
faqs.a: Yes. Rebuild uses the standard URL encoding rules, so characters like & and = inside values are safely escaped.

labels.invalidLabel: That does not look like a valid absolute URL. It must start with http:// or https://.
